paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage hands us. Four hundred prophets said what the king wanted to hear, and one man said what God told him. Micaiah's answer to the messenger is the whole lesson: "As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever my God tells me." (2 Chronicles 18:13) A crowd saying the same thing doesn't make it true, and a pleasant word isn't the same as a true one.

Now look at Ahab. He hated the one voice that told him the truth, and he threw that man in prison. Micaiah's reply to him was, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." (2 Chronicles 18:27) Ahab disguised himself and went into battle anyway, and at sunset he died. (2 Chronicles 18:29, 34) I think the loudest lesson here is that you can dodge the messenger, but you can't dodge the message.

So what do we do with that, baker? Be like Jehoshaphat and ask, "Please inquire first for the word of the LORD." (2 Chronicles 18:4) Check what you're hearing against God's Word, even when it sounds good and everybody around you is nodding. And when you cry out, the LORD helps, like He helped Jehoshaphat when the chariot commanders turned on him. (2 Chronicles 18:31) The story isn't over, though, because Jehoshaphat's still got more coming.
